claims.rationale: Pre-cutoff studies demonstrated that the coiled-coil interaction of GATAD2A (p66alpha) with MBD2 is critical for NuRD complex recruitment and globin gene silencing, supporting the post-cutoff discovery that perturbing GATAD2A derepresses fetal hemoglobin.

EIF2AK1 (HRI) is an erythroid-enriched kinase that modifies the phenotypic severity of beta-thalassemia and activates the Atf4 pathway during erythropoiesis, supporting its establishment as a regulator of fetal hemoglobin.

ATF4 functions downstream of heme-regulated eIF2alpha kinase (HRI) and is required for definitive erythropoiesis, indicating a functional regulatory role in the erythroid stress and globin expression axis.

ZBTB7A (LRF) was established prior to the cutoff as an essential downstream target of GATA1 in erythroid development and differentiation, supporting its prospective role in erythroid globin gene regulation.

refusals.reason: There is no functional or physical evidence prior to the cutoff connecting ASH1L to fetal hemoglobin regulation or erythroid globin switching.
Although CHD3 is a component of the NuRD complex, pre-cutoff evidence links globin repression specifically to CHD4 rather than CHD3.
Pre-cutoff evidence does not establish DNMT1 perturbation as a novel post-cutoff regulator of fetal hemoglobin distinct from prior DNA demethylation studies.
No pre-cutoff evidence demonstrates that perturbing DNMT3A specifically regulates fetal hemoglobin expression in human erythroid cells.
Available pre-cutoff data provide no functional connection between DNMT3B and the regulation of fetal hemoglobin.
No pre-cutoff evidence indicates that EHMT1 perturbation regulates fetal hemoglobin in human erythroid cells.
Pre-cutoff literature in the graph does not provide functional evidence that perturbing EHMT2 establishes fetal hemoglobin regulation in human erythroid cells.
EIF2AK2 (PKR) is broadly expressed and lacks pre-cutoff evidence linking it to erythroid-specific fetal hemoglobin regulation.
EIF2AK3 (PERK) lacks evidence of an erythroid-specific functional role in fetal hemoglobin regulation prior to the cutoff.
Pre-cutoff records do not show a functional role for EIF2AK4 (GCN2) in regulating fetal hemoglobin expression.
EIF2S1 is a core translation initiation factor whose general perturbation affects global translation and viability without established specific fetal hemoglobin regulation.
Pre-cutoff evidence connects EPAS1 to general hypoxia responses rather than specific regulation of fetal hemoglobin in human erythroid cells.
Although FOXO3 participates in erythroid maturation and oxidative stress resistance, pre-cutoff evidence does not support a specific role in fetal hemoglobin regulation.
Pre-cutoff NuRD complex globin silencing studies specifically implicate GATAD2A (p66alpha) rather than GATAD2B (p66beta).
HDAC2 was already functionally demonstrated to regulate fetal hemoglobin in human erythroid cells prior to the cutoff date, precluding a novel post-cutoff establishment.
No pre-cutoff publications or functional measurements in the graph link HIC2 to erythroid biology or fetal hemoglobin regulation.
No evidence prior to the cutoff date links IGF2BP1 to the regulation of fetal hemoglobin in human erythroid cells.
The role of KDM1A (LSD1) in fetal hemoglobin derepression was already investigated prior to the cutoff date and graph records lack novel supporting evidence.
There is no pre-cutoff functional evidence connecting KMT5A to fetal hemoglobin regulation in erythroid cells.
LIN28B was already established prior to the cutoff date as an inducer of fetal hemoglobin in adult human erythroblasts.
Pre-cutoff publications for MAP3K7 focus on inflammatory and survival signaling without evidence of fetal hemoglobin regulation.
No pre-cutoff evidence indicates that MAPK1 perturbation selectively regulates fetal hemoglobin expression.
The requirement of MBD2 in NuRD-mediated globin gene silencing was already established prior to the cutoff date.
Pre-cutoff studies show that MBD3-NuRD complexes are distinct from MBD2-NuRD and do not demonstrate fetal hemoglobin regulation upon MBD3 perturbation.
No pre-cutoff evidence establishes that perturbing MTA1 regulates fetal hemoglobin in human erythroid cells.
Although MTA2 is a core NuRD subunit, pre-cutoff data do not demonstrate that its individual perturbation alters fetal hemoglobin.
Pre-cutoff evidence does not support a functional role for MTA3 in fetal hemoglobin regulation.
NFE2 is a well-characterized erythroid transcription factor that is not functionally established as a regulator of fetal globin switching.
Pre-cutoff records do not provide evidence linking NFIX to fetal hemoglobin expression or globin gene switching.
Pre-cutoff data available in the graph do not provide sufficient functional evidence to establish NR2C1 as a post-cutoff fetal hemoglobin regulator.
Pre-cutoff records in the graph do not establish that perturbing NR2C2 regulates fetal hemoglobin in human erythroid cells.
No pre-cutoff evidence connects PGRMC1 to fetal hemoglobin regulation or erythroid gene expression.
RBBP4 is a ubiquitous histone-binding NuRD subunit lacking evidence that its specific perturbation regulates fetal hemoglobin.
No pre-cutoff functional evidence demonstrates that perturbing RBBP7 changes fetal hemoglobin levels in human erythroid cells.
Pre-cutoff data for SIRT1 relate to general oxidative stress and deacetylase activity without evidence of fetal hemoglobin regulation.
Pre-cutoff records do not support a role for SMAD1 in the direct regulation of fetal hemoglobin in human erythroid cells.
No pre-cutoff evidence indicates that perturbing SMAD5 alters fetal hemoglobin expression.
TAL1 is a master transcription factor required for general erythropoiesis whose perturbation does not specifically establish fetal globin regulation.
Pre-cutoff literature associates TET2 with hematopoiesis and myeloid malignancies without evidence of fetal hemoglobin regulation.
No pre-cutoff evidence demonstrates that VHL perturbation regulates fetal hemoglobin expression in human erythroid cells.
There is no pre-cutoff functional evidence linking the methyl-CpG binding protein ZBTB33 (Kaiso) to fetal hemoglobin regulation.
Pre-cutoff records provide no evidence that ZNF143 is involved in fetal hemoglobin regulation or erythroid globin switching.
No pre-cutoff publications or functional assays in the graph link ZNF410 to erythroid gene expression or fetal hemoglobin regulation.

notes: 12 of 16 contamination traps passed. These pass by construction under the refusal rule, so a pass shows the time slice held rather than that the system reasoned well. A failure would mean post-cutoff evidence reached the forecast.

Correctly refused and also in the ground truth: ATF4, DNMT1, EHMT1, EHMT2, EIF2AK1, GATAD2A, HDAC2, HIC2, LIN28B, MBD2, MTA2, NFIX, RBBP4, TAL1, ZBTB7A, ZNF410. These count as correct refusals and as missed forecasts at the same time, which is the honest description: the pre-cutoff evidence did not support the claim, and the field found it anyway.
Language-model row. A refusal carries no confidence from the model and is entered at 0 for the calibration error. The cost lens does not apply: the model is not asked for a therapeutic route.
